concept.name: Swing high
concept.definition: A local price peak — a high flanked by lower highs on either side — marking the point where an advance stalled and turned down. Swing highs (peaks) and swing lows (troughs) are the basic building blocks from which trend direction is read in classical technical analysis.
concept.intuition: The top of one 'zig' before the market 'zags' back down.
concept.mechanics: Discretionary analysts mark visible reaction peaks on the chart; rule-based definitions require a bar whose high exceeds the highs of a fixed number of bars on each side (e.g., two). Successive swing highs are compared — higher, lower, or equal — to classify trend structure, and old swing highs often serve as reference resistance.
concept.failure_modes: The lookback that defines a swing is arbitrary, so different analysts mark different swings; minor swing highs are constantly exceeded and re-marked, making the concept scale-dependent.
concept.misconceptions: That a swing high is a precise resistance price; it is better treated as an approximate zone, since technical analysis is not an exact science.
concept.example: A stock rallies to 55, declines to 52, and rallies again: 55 is a swing high that later acts as a reference resistance level.

citations.source: Fidelity Investments — Basic concepts of trend
